newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures end higher on steady cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures end higher on steady cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished higher Tuesday from Friday's settlements on steady cash market prices in the western U.S., brokers and traders.
Amid expectations of lower output from hydroelectric system in the Northwest after summer's fish flush, short-term physical prices, especially in the Southwest, rose, they said.
"PV (Palo Verde) picked up steam on stronger next-day prices," said one Houston trader, adding tighter supply in the Northwest also affected the Southwest market.
The New York Mercantile Exchange was closed Monday in observance of the U.S. Labor Day holiday.

October California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled up five cents at $15.75 per megawatt hour (MWh). November COB finished up 10 cents at $16.50. Deferred COB contracts ended flat to five cents higher.
October PV futures settled up 30 cents at $16.75. November PV finished up 20 cents at $15.60. Active outer-month PV contracts ended mixed.

Although the electricity complex received a slight lift today, a number of players still viewed short-term prospects somewhat bearishly based on the fact that overall electricity usage will drop as autumn approachs.
"There'll be some more down side," another Houston trader said.
NYMEX estimated 21 COB and 16 PV contracts changed hands today.
